_why: Per-plugin overrides, merged onto the plan derived from a scan.
The scan probes every control from the unit's default state, and for a
passive EQ that state is *flat* — which is to say idle. A flat EQ passes
audio through its amplifier without asking it to do anything, so it
measures clean and every control shows a 1.0x THD span. The Hitsville EQ
read 0.00000% flat and 30.90% with its seven bands and output gain at
+8 dB. Nothing about the scan could have found that: the saturation is
not on any single control, it is in the unit being *worked*.
So these entries say how to put a unit under load before measuring it.
'engage' pins are applied for the level sweep; 'engage_axes' are then
swept one at a time, because how far a band is pushed is the drive.

UADx Hitsville EQ.why: Seven bands at +-8 dB plus an output Gain. Flat it is silent-clean; boosted it reaches 30.9% THD, odd-dominant.

UADx Hitsville EQ Mastering.why: Seven bands as L<n>-Gain, each 0..+8 dB and boost-only, paired with an L<n>-Dip/Pk switch that decides whether that gain is a peak or a dip. Boosting the gains while the bands sit on Dip drives the signal DOWN: the first attempt measured 0.006% engaged against 0.0196% flat, less distortion for more knob. Both halves have to be set.

UADx Pultec EQP-1A.why: The famous move is boosting and attenuating the low band at once. Both curves run through the output amplifier, which is what saturates.

UADx Pultec MEQ-5.why: Midrange Pultec: the two peaks and the dip all feed the same output stage.

UADx Pultec HLF-3C.why: Filters only, no boost and no output amplifier to push. Engaging it changes the response, not the distortion. Measured flat and expected to stay clean; the entry exists to record that this was checked rather than missed.

UADx Manley Massive Passive.why: Passive EQ with an active make-up amplifier: the bands attenuate and the amplifier makes it back up, so boosting the bands is what drives it.

UADx Manley Massive Passive MST.why: Mastering version of the same circuit.
